7.3.2 Selecting the RESET Delay Time
The TPS3808 has three options for setting the RESET delay time as shown in Figure 7-2. Figure 7-2 (a) shows
the configuration for a fixed 300ms typical delay time by tying CT to VDD; use a resistor from 40kΩ to 200kΩ.
Resistor selection does not impact the supply current. Figure 7-2 (b) shows a fixed 20ms delay time by leaving
the CT pin open. Figure 7-2 (c) shows a ground referenced capacitor connected to CT for a user-defined program
time from 1.25ms to 10s.
      3.3V                                                3.3V                                                3.3V

                     SENSE VDD                                        SENSE VDD                                            SENSE VDD

              50kΩ
                     TPS3808G33                                       TPS3808G33                                           TPS3808G33


                     CT     RESET                                     CT     RESET                                         CT    RESET

                     300ms Delay                                       20ms Delay
                                                                                                                             175
                          (a)                                               (b)                                                (c)

                                 Figure 7-2. Configuration Used to Set the RESET Delay Time

The capacitor CT must be ≥ 100pF nominal value for the TPS3808xxx to recognize that the capacitor is present.
Calculate the capacitor value for a given delay time using Equation 1.

             CT nF = tD s − 0.5 × 10−3 s × 175                                                                                                     (1)

The time an on-chip precision 220nA current source takes to charge the external capacitor to 1.23V determines
the reset delay time. When a RESET is asserted, the capacitor is discharged. When the RESET conditions are
cleared, the internal current source is enabled and begins to charge the external capacitor. When the voltage on
this capacitor reaches 1.23V, RESET is deasserted. Note that a low-leakage type capacitor such as a ceramic
must be used, and that stray capacitance around this pin can cause errors in the reset delay time.
7.3.3 Manual RESET (MR) Input
The manual reset (MR) input allows a processor or other logic circuits to initiate a reset. A logic low (0.3 VDD) on
MR causes RESET to assert. After MR returns to a logic high and SENSE is above its reset threshold, RESET
is de-asserted after the user-defined reset delay expires. Note that MR is internally tied to VDD using a 90kΩ
resistor, so this pin can be left unconnected if MR is not used.
See Figure 7-3 for how to use MR to monitor multiple system voltages. Note that if the logic signal driving MR
does not go fully to VDD, there is some additional current draw into VDD as a result of the internal pullup resistor
on MR. To minimize current draw, use a logic-level FET, as in Figure 7-4.
